subject: MSA & Order Form — request to roll back assignment covenant; evaluation license wording
messages:
From: Susan Li <susan.li@novaprod.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@novaprod.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form — request to roll back assignment covenant and propose eval license wording

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the model catalog. We’re working through the MSA + Order Form redlines internally and our legal team has pushed back on Redwood’s proposed assignment language in Section 7.3 (the draft asks for assignment of outputs where we use the model to generate product content).

To avoid derailing terms, Novaprod would like to:
- Roll back the assignment ask to a non-exclusive license for output (we can accept a narrow license for productization but not assignment).
- Add a short-term evaluation/trial license carveout that explicitly allows Novaprod to use outputs for product evaluation and UAT without granting rights for retraining/derivative model use.
- Provide a limited feedback license for telemetry that we can anonymize.

I attached our redlines (novaprod_redlines_v3.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) swap the assignment provision for a limited license (we’d like suggested language), and
2) provide sample language for an evaluation/trial license and a feedback license that limits retraining and model ingestion.

We’re aiming to get terms resolved before the procurement review next Thursday. If it helps, LegalOps is available for a short 30-minute call to align.

Thanks,
Susan Li
Head of Procurement, Novaprod Systems
legalops@novaprod.com

Attachment: novaprod_redlines_v3.docx (redline doc, summary of requested changes)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Susan Li <susan.li@novaprod.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — request to roll back assignment covenant and propose eval license wording

Hi Susan — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines.

High level: Redwood is open to moving away from an outright assignment and toward a narrowly scoped license for outputs, but we need to preserve strong protections against model retraining and derivative claims. Below are the proposed next steps we can take now:

1) Draft suggested replacement language: non-exclusive, perpetual license to use/distribute customer-generated outputs for the customer’s products (no assignment) + explicit carveout stating outputs cannot be used to retrain Redwood models or incorporated into Redwood model weights.
2) Evaluation/trial license: a timebox (e.g., 60 days) permitting product evaluation/UAT with outputs restricted from being used beyond productization unless a separate license is agreed.
3) Feedback license / telemetry: accept collection of telemetry and anonymized feedback under a limited, revocable license for the purpose of improving service quality, with a default 90-day retention and an option for Novaprod to opt-out of feedback ingestion for retraining.

I’m attaching a short draft response for legal to review (redwood_response_draft.docx). Karthik — can you and Legal please prioritize markup of the attached and advise on acceptable fallback language if Novaprod insists on assignment wording? Marissa — can you coordinate a 30-min legal-only sync with Novaprod for Thurs morning PT?

Proposed immediate asks for Novaprod:
- Confirm whether 60-day evaluation window works;
- Confirm they will accept anonymized telemetry and the 90-day retention proposal;
- If they insist on assignment, provide a targeted list of product scenarios that trigger assignment (we may be able to narrow).

Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood_response_draft.docx (draft replacement language and questions for legal)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — request to roll back assignment covenant and propose eval license wording

Irene / Marissa — quick legal take (high level):

- We should avoid assignment language; counter with a narrowly tailored license. Assignment is a large precedent risk.
- Proposed legal markup suggestions (see attachment legal_markup_msa_redlines.pdf):
  * Replace "assignment" with: "Customer is granted a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs in Customer’s Products and Services; no rights to retrain, fine-tune, or incorporate Outputs into model weights are granted to Customer."
  * Evaluation license: time-limited (45–60 days), expressly not a license to retrain or to sublicense; include a clause that any outputs used beyond evaluation require a written amendment.
  * Feedback license: limited grant to use customer-submitted feedback for service quality improvements, strictly on an anonymized and aggregated basis, and not for model retraining unless Customer explicitly opts in.
  * Telemetry / retention: 90 days default, with option to request deletion and a separate SLA for telemetry retrieval for audit.

If Novaprod insists on assignment language we should: 1) request their use-cases that require assignment, 2) propose escrow or other mitigations (e.g., explicit carveouts, a high fee for assignment, or a limited-scope assignment tied to a specific asset), and 3) escalate to commercial leadership.

I recommend we send the marked draft back to Susan with the above replacement language and ask Novaprod to confirm the 60-day evaluation window and telemetry opt-out mechanics.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_markup_msa_redlines.pdf (legal line edits and comments)

From: Susan Li <susan.li@novaprod.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@novaprod.com>
Date: 2025-10-17T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — request to roll back assignment covenant and propose eval license wording

Thanks Irene and Karthik — that read-through is helpful. Novaprod is willing to accept non-exclusive license language instead of assignment provided Redwood can supply the exact replacement paragraphs for the MSA and a clear definition of the evaluation window.

Answers:
- 60 days for evaluation is acceptable.
- Telemetry: Novaprod will accept anonymized telemetry and a 90-day retention as long as there is a process to request deletion for specific datasets (we’ll capture that in procurement).
- Feedback / retrain opt-out: Novaprod would like a single-line opt-out checkbox explicitly preventing Redwood from using submitted feedback for model retraining absent a separate written agreement.

Can you send a legal-ready redline (we don’t need a call yet — LegalOps will review your redline and revert if necessary). I attached our counter redlines for reference (counter_redlines.docx).

If possible, please include suggested DocuSign-ready clause snippets so procurement can move quickly.

Best,
Susan
Head of Procurement, Novaprod Systems

Attachment: counter_redlines.docx (procurement’s counter with explanation notes)
